title: 恢复 native Tool Registry / Tool Search 与确定性 Image/Search 能力路由

root_cause.tool_registry: Tool Search derived its catalog from one Agent-visible snapshot intersected with a separate process-global snapshot. That excluded inherited Agent-scope definitions, admitted same-named local/global ambiguity, and allowed a stale name to reach rc.7 tools.restrict(), whose contract accepts only the current Agent's inherited restrictable schema.
root_cause.reconcile: The same stale catalog was reused while replacing restrictions after tools/change, so a late registration race could throw the native unknown-global error instead of failing open.
root_cause.search: The Tool Search component also patched rc.7 away from the accepted deepseek-official Provider to a second gpt-responses Provider using another model and an insecure HTTP endpoint.
root_cause.routing: Generic operation guidance did not state the explicit webpage-intent boundary, leaving Browser/CDP open as an accidental fallback for first-party image, native search, or attachment work.

resolution.tool_registry: The component now uses the native per-Agent restriction seam itself to distinguish the Agent's own unrestrictable definitions from its current inherited schema, then intersects every allow list after lifting the previous restriction. Agent-local Schedule definitions remain direct, and Tool Search is omitted when no long-tail definition needs disclosure.
resolution.reconcile: agent/created, restored request headers, late register/unregister, tools/change and disposal all rebuild from the current native Agent view. Installation/reconciliation failures remove Tool Search and its restriction best-effort, preserve the native surface, and do not block the registry mutation.
resolution.search: The conflicting Provider source, export, tests, authority, dependencies and patch rows were deleted. The only configured path remains rc.7 web_search -> deepseek-official -> E_MATE_SEARCH_KEY_DEEPSEEK -> https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic/v1 -> deepseek-v4-flash.
resolution.routing: imagegen and web_search remain directly visible first-party tools. Chinese image intents are discovery aliases for imagegen only; Browser/CDP is limited to the user's latest explicit request to read or operate a visible webpage.
